summary.intent: Debug two Claude Code tool errors (blank statusline and a per-turn Stop hook MODULE_NOT_FOUND from a missing GSD hook), then run the full GSD plan→execute→ship pipeline for Phase 61 — adding an AAD-bound AES-256-GCM seal primitive with a frozen cross-language KAT to both the TypeScript and Rust crypto packages.
summary.outcome: Both tool errors fixed (statusline.js renamed to .cjs; GSD reinstalled to v1.6.0 restoring missing hooks and manifest); Phase 61 fully delivered as PR #576 with 5 plans across 4 waves, 197 TS + 97 Rust tests green, 28/28 CI checks passing, 6 review threads resolved, and merged to main.

repo: The project has `"type": "module"` in package.json — all .js Claude hook files are treated as ESM. Hooks that use require() must use the .cjs extension or Node throws ReferenceError on startup, silently blanking the statusline.

GSD hooks are gitignored (.gitignore covers .claude/hooks/gsd-*) and are only installed by the GSD installer — git cannot restore them. A partial/broken GSD install in the main tree will silently wire missing hooks into settings.local.json.

GSD package is @opengsd/gsd-core, installed via npx. When the main-tree install is a broken fragment (missing gsd-tools.cjs, manifest, most workflows), re-run with auto-resolved --remove to let stale files regenerate cleanly: `npx @opengsd/gsd-core@1.6.0 -- gsd-core --claude --local`.

TS crypto tests must live at packages/crypto/src/__tests__/ — vitest include is ['src/**/*.ts']. The path packages/crypto/__tests__/ is outside the include and vitest will never discover it; CONTEXT.md had the wrong path.

scripts/check-vector-parity.sh has a hardcoded EXPECTED_VECTORS array. Adding a new tests/vectors/crypto/*.json file without registering it there causes the CI parity-check step to fail even when both TS and Rust tests pass.

Fixed-IV KAT vectors must target the lower-level encryptAesGcmAad (not sealAesGcmAad, which mints a random IV and cannot produce a fixed ciphertext). This mirrors how the existing aes-gcm.json vectors test encrypt_aes_gcm rather than seal_aes_gcm.
CodeRabbit CLI `--base main` uses local main, which can be stale and inflate the diff scope (661 files vs 44). Always use `--base origin/main` to match the actual PR scope.

main branch protection has required_signatures: False and 0 required reviews. The only ruleset targets tag creation, not branch PRs. Unsigned commits do not block merges here — prior memory claiming otherwise was stale.
The GSD commit helper can report commit_failed while the commit actually lands. Always verify with `git log --oneline -1`; never blindly retry based on the helper's exit status.
github-actions[bot] pushes a chore(release) commit to the branch after PR creation and after each subsequent push. Always git fetch + rebase before the next push or it will be rejected.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL error) — patch the PR body via `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file` instead.
CodeRabbit may show 'Review skipped' transiently immediately after PR creation before its analysis completes. Re-poll rather than treating it as confirmation that no review will be posted.

code.finding: Existing encryptAesGcm uses `new Uint8Array(key)` copy WITHOUT zeroizing afterward — this is the established project pattern. New AAD variants intentionally mirror it; zeroizing only the new variants would create inconsistency.

New cross-language KAT file. Must assert aad_vectors.length === 4 AND role-set [1,2,3,4] explicitly (not just iterate) — a for...of over an empty array passes vacuously. Same for seal_vectors: assert exact count, not just length > 0.

Cross-language KAT for AAD builder and AEAD seal. Envelope-order pin added: verifies that sealed output splits correctly as [12-byte IV][ciphertext+tag] by round-tripping via unseal_aes_gcm_aad on the split pieces.
EXPECTED_VECTORS array is hardcoded — any new tests/vectors/crypto/*.json file must be registered here explicitly or CI parity fails silently even with passing unit tests on both sides.
Renamed from statusline.js to force Node.js to treat it as CommonJS (require() calls) despite project-level `"type": "module"`. The .cjs extension overrides the package-level ESM default.

workflow: GSD plan-phase: PATTERNS.md is not auto-committed by the plan-phase workflow — the orchestrator must commit it explicitly after the pattern-mapper subagent returns.

GSD execute-phase: disable worktrees for sequential phases where plans read/write shared files in order (e.g. node-aad.json written by plan 01, read by plan 02). Worktrees lack node_modules and require a slow pnpm install per wave; running sequentially on the main tree with a warm cache is faster and more reliable.

Ultracode adversarial plan verification: a multi-lens workflow review caught the vacuous-pass KAT gap (TS vector arrays iterated without length assertions) before execution, enabling a cheap plan-level fix rather than a post-execute re-plan on security-critical crypto.
A security review subagent that independently re-derives a KAT ciphertext via OpenSSL constitutes a true third-implementation proof — stronger confidence than checking test output alone.

When AFK for an autonomous pipeline, disable commit signing locally (`git config --local commit.gpgsign false`) to prevent 1Password biometric prompts from hanging subagent commits. Re-enable on return with `git config --local --unset commit.gpgsign`.

The GSD plan verifier's two-gate design (deterministic script gate 5a + hunk-verification table 5b) provides defense-in-depth: the script gate cannot be shortcut by the LLM filling in 'verified: yes' without an actual content-presence check.

friction: GSD commit helper false-negatives on every commit throughout the session — reports commit_failed while commits actually land, requiring a `git log --oneline -1` verification call after each commit.
CodeRabbit CLI `--base main` (local stale branch) inflated diff scope to 661 files vs the actual 44-file PR, triggering a file-limit error and requiring a re-run with `--base origin/main`.
CodeRabbit showed 'Review skipped' immediately after PR creation (transient), causing false confidence that no threads would land; 5 threads appeared on the next poll cycle.
The Stop hook MODULE_NOT_FOUND error (gsd-context-monitor.js) fired silently on every turn from the start of the session — noisy but non-blocking, with no obvious error surfaced in the UI.
The statusline went blank with no visible error message; the ESM/CJS root cause only surfaced when the hook script was manually executed.
The background CI check poll exited early when only 2 checks were registered on a new head, requiring a second manual poll to get the settled verdict.
The release bot pushes a chore(release) commit after PR creation and after each subsequent push, requiring a fetch+rebase before every push in the ship loop to avoid rejection.
Greptile posted a COMMENTED review rather than a pull-request-review, requiring separate thread-resolution handling outside the standard CodeRabbit flow.
